msItem.title: Lǝfāfa ṣǝdq
msItem.note: Some parts of the work have been copied out of order, most notably, the Prayer Concerning the Agony of Death has been swapped with two Prayers for the Journey to Heaven.

msItem.title: Mangada samāy
msItem.explicit: ወለመንበረ፡ ስብሐቲሁ፡ ለእግዚአብሔር፡ ዘሐነጸ፡ ጽርሖ፡ ወአልቦ፡ ዘየአምሮ፡ ዘእንበለ፡ አብ፡ ባሕቲቱ፡ ወዘእንበለ፡ ክርስቶስ፡ ወልዱ፡ ወመንገሱ፡ ቅዱስ፡ኦመሓሪ፡ መሐረንኢ፡ ወስረይ፡ ኃጢትየ፡ ሊተ፡ ለገብርከ፡ ኃይለ፡ ጊዮርጊስ፡ ወልደ፡ ሩፋኤል፡
msItem.note: Only two prayers have been included instead of the usual seven.

msItem.title: Two parts of Lǝfāfa ṣǝdq copied together.
msItem.incipit: በስመ፡ አብ፡ በብርሃን፡ ስሙ፡ ለእግዚአብሔር፡ ኢይትፈለጥ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወምድር፡ ፯መላእክት፡ ብርሃናውያን፡ እለ፡ ይነብሩ፡ ታሕተ፡ መንጦላዕቱ፡ ቅዱስ፡

decoNote.desc: Three black and red crosses with interlaced border above and below at the top of the first strip.
Three black and red crosses with decorative border above and below at the top of the second strip.
Three black and red crosses with interlaced border with eyes above and below at the bottom of the third strip.

item.desc: The words ቄል, ኤል, and ሄል are written between the three crosses in each miniature.

decoNote.desc: A leather case on which is embossed with gold letters the title Lefafa zedcho libr. superstiz. etiopico.

history.provenance: According to a letter from Ṭobiya Giyorgis Gäbrä Ǝgziʾabǝḥer to Stefano Borgia dated 19 December 1788, Ṭobiyā, who found the scroll in the library at Santo Stefano de' Mori, sent it to Borgia along with a description of its contents.
history.acquisition: The Borgia collection entered the Vatican Library during the pontificate of Leo XIII (1878-1903).
